movie_name: Portrait of a Lady on Fire

reviews.text: With elements of the surreal and supernatural dotted in among the erotic, the film's panoply of extraordinary images adds up to a haunting melancholic masterclass.
reviews.author: Calum Baker

reviews.text: Claire Mathon’s stunning cinematography is achingly beautiful to gaze upon. Each frame is worthy of being hung in an art gallery, and each shot conveys so much meaning.
reviews.author: Bianca Garner

reviews.text: They say memory is the poet’s choice of love. After watching this masterpiece, I suspect that the present moment is the artist’s choice of love.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Director Céline Sciamma’s romantic feature celebrates the burning desires between two women with patience and tenderness unlike any film has shown in recent years.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: Add two tantalizing performances from Noémie Merlant and Adèle Haenel, and you have yourself one of the most romantic, beautiful films of the decade...
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: The film links several interesting themes: the role of women artists at that time, lesbianism, abortion, social canons and their hypocrisy. There are at least two aspects of the women painters that are well and correspond to historical facts.
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: Watching the two women grow closer together is almost intoxicating, even with the devastating knowledge that they’ll never truly be able to have what they want.
reviews.author: Patricia Karounos

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire, is a triumph. Few romance movies capture the totality of love, loss, and remembrance in the way Sciamma does in this film.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: In contrast to a film like 2013’s Blue is the Warmest Color, there is no exploitative nudity, no male gaze or overt sexuality. And yet there’s rarely a moment that’s not subtly charged with eroticism.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: Things kick off simply, if not innocently, in Céline Sciamma’s masterful period film.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Every artist begins with a blank canvas. It is what they do with it that defines them. With Portrait Of A Lady On Fire, Céline Sciamma has painted her masterpiece.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: The period piece is a mesmerizing story about desire and heartbreak, and one of the best queer films of the year.
reviews.author: Michael Cuby

reviews.text: This intelligent and sensuous film is special. An intimate and delicate study of how two people can fall in love.
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: Every shot feels as if it was painted on a canvas. Love and romance are not the same thing, and it is subtly shown in this movie that surrounds the lack of freedom there is in secrets. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: Portrait Of A Lady On Fire is passionate, elegant, and elemental.
reviews.author: Merryn Johns

reviews.text: An abortion subplot allows for a scene of artistically inspired exploitation that breaks the film.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: It's a film that acknowledges the limits of reality even as Sciamma finds overriding freedom in her characters yearnings, making, as one character observes, not the lover's choice, but the poet's in telling this story.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The plot reveals itself with an assured poetic tone that never falters. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: What works comes less from the script and more from the presence and power of the two beautiful protagonists. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernando E. Juan Lima

reviews.text: ...a sumptuous, haunting love story with moments of dynamism...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Once in a while there is a work of art so specific, so complex, so new in its oldness and old in its newness, that it moves the craft, our craft, to another level of seeing.
reviews.author: Drew Gregory

reviews.text: While it says much about the female gaze - both as painter and painted, watcher and watched - that doesn't stop it from sagging in its final act.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: [A] deconstruction of the male gaze, bringing forth a new lens through which to view women's agency and historic contributions to art... wrapped in a gentle yet painful love story.
reviews.author: Laura Potier

reviews.text: Unfolds as a liquid painting, shades of honey, earth, and time, with a soundtrack burning off all that is unnecessary.
reviews.author: Milana Vujkov

reviews.text: The movie is a deeply affecting memory piece where even present-tense pleasure is edged with sadness and regret.
reviews.author: Yasmin Omar

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is a brilliant and visually stunning meditation on the meaning of art and love, as well as the choices we make as artists and lovers.
reviews.author: Aviva Dove-Viebahn

reviews.text: In a film filled with arresting images, none is better than its final shot. Haunting and raw.
reviews.author: Luiz Oliveira

reviews.text: Through this acceptance of women's flaws, the most important message of the film becomes judgement is faulty, fleeting, and unsustainable, while love, even neglected and unfed, lives on for a lifetime.
reviews.author: Sara Century

reviews.text: Few of us have figured out how to upend over a century of defining and reinforcing what cinema is. Sciamma did it.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is set 260 years in the past, but the sentiments of its story are extremely modern. It's also as great, if not better, than any movie with a male focus, and continued proof that women's voices deserve to be heard.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: There is a joyful vivrancy about the film. They fully accept their fate, laid out by period and society. Yet they enjoy their few days together and remember it forever. It's super life affirming and uplifting, rather than sad.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: With gorgeous cinematography, [and] a beautiful script that shows off the French language at its very best...Céline Sciamma's new film is easily one of the best of the year.
reviews.author: Nicole Ackman

reviews.text: It's high art to the highest degree, a movie that is great now, will be great in 50 years, will be great in 150 years.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: There's almost no single moment in Portrait of a Lady on Fire that couldn't be captured, mounted, and hung on a wall as high art.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: There are many great acting moments in this film, but you should especially savor the final shot, the long close-up of Haenel in profile. Put simply, it's why we go to the movies.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Metaphorical and melancholic, Céline Sciamma's masterpiece is a slow burn period romance that takes its time to draw you in. But once it does, there's no looking back.
reviews.author: Renuka Vyavahare

reviews.text: [Sciamma] frames Marianne and Héloïse's developing relationship with such exquisite skill that almost every detail throbs with meaning and emotion.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Both passionate and delicate, Celine Sciamma's breath-stoppingly beautiful period film, set in 18th-century Brittany, centres on a painter...
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: [On a] deeper level, Portrait of a Lady on Fire is about filmmaking itself. Marianne the artist and Héloïse the model are the director and the actor, respectively, for the painting. It's a movie that plays inside of the movie.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: Both Noemie Merlant and Adele Haenel are flawlessly brilliant as two women who are blissfully in love yet rattled by their love's prolonged conclusion.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Céline Sciama condones the almost voyeuristic viewpoint in this type of film and instead has the camera serve as an accomplice to what we see. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: An elegant, endlessly gorgeous piece of film that hits you right in the centre of your heart.
reviews.author: Andrew Gaudion

reviews.text: The development of the film is hidden under an apparent simplicity, where the tension falls into the deep gaze of their confused protagonists. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gabriela Meza

reviews.text: Crackles and dances like the titular flames, as dangerous and unpredictable as it is beautiful and fascinating.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: French director Céline Sciamma's fourth feature film... ventures into period cinema in a new way, with expressive vigor and meticulous attention to scenographic details. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: Even though Sciamma has certain technical skills and a stylish touch, the movie's premise of a manless "utopia" is barren and, frankly, stupid.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: [Writer/director Celine] Sciamma is blessed with two lead actors whose haunted round eyes and exquisitely calibrated performances offer portraits of studied desperation, crushed beneath centuries of societal expectations.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire has been crafted with a painter's eye, a poet's tongue and a musician's control over emotion. As art imitates life, and life imitates art, Sciamma gives us arguably the greatest love story ever told on cinema.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: That Portrait of a Lady on Fire is as much concerned with uncovering the story as it is with pinpointing who it is that gets to tell that story, is revealed in tiny bursts of detail that somehow seem to contain a lifetime of information.
reviews.author: Poulomi Das

reviews.text: A passionate, poetic, and devastating film that comprehends love in a profound, intelligent manner, challenging time and society rules in the process. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: A pitch-perfect blend of exquisite visual storytelling and raw emotion, with two indelible performances from its lead actresses.
reviews.author: Adam Lubitow

reviews.text: It is endowed with an ethereal lyricism, with images of vigorous invoice that speak about love, art and memory. There are beautiful shots, composed like a alla prima painted canvas. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Portrait is a triumph of auteurism.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: This critic would struggle to list a film, in recent memory, that is so elegantly and beautifully assembled and executed.
reviews.author: Caitlin Kennedy

reviews.text: Smart, quiet and pulsating...the performances are as rich as they are beautiful...
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Recognizes the hope and futility that accompany the attempt to capture another person's essence, in love or in art.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: The women savour every moment they can with an intensity that's as joyful as it is heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: A tremendously intimate, gradual burn of forbidden love.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: From the soulful gazes of her film's two protagonists, to the repeated references to women bemoaning the powerlessness of their positions, Sciamma's "Portrait of a Lady on Fire" is a testament to the depths of feminine desire.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: ...an exquisite love story.
reviews.author: Anupama Chopra

reviews.text: a beautifully mounted drama about forbidden love that has every reason to be an intense emotional experience, but somehow never quite shakes free from its carefully designed and modulated aesthetic
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Sciamma's work joins a select group of texts that brilliantly thematise the power of the image - either through painting, drawing or photography.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Beautifully shot, perfectly timed, and with breathtaking performances from the two leads, this film is a masterpiece in cinema.
reviews.author: Danny Brogan

reviews.text: Director Celine Sciamma has made something far more than a period costume flick. She's made a romance portraying explosive longing through steady glances and brief caresses.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: I want you to experience this truly beautiful, heartbreaking, love-affirming film. I want you to witness its empathy and care, and I want you to be swept away by Noémie Merlant and Adèle Haenel.
reviews.author: Andrew F. Peirce

reviews.text: If you ever have a chance to see this surpassingly beautiful film on the big screen, don't miss it.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is a must-see French film about love, art, and the inevitabilities of life.
reviews.author: Karen Rought

reviews.text: It's a symphony of artful images. I'll let more confident (or less male) critics comment on whether Sciamma is pursuing some "female gaze" distinct from what my lying eyes tell me and just say it's a beautiful, deeply sensual film.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: A remarkably affecting tale of forbidden gay love, and also one of the most profound, and accurate, depictions of the artistic process ever put to film.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: The female solidarity is striking. The women know that their relationship is doomed from the start. Not only is it impossible to imagine a lesbian life together, but Marianne is actually creating the object that will separate them forever.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: Sciamma seems to be inventing love anew, giving us something at once familiar, like the lingering memory of lovers long past, and vibrantly, thrillingly new.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Though an unabashedly gorgeous movie, "Portrait" is not an easy film. It is deliberately slow and hypnotic, demanding you adjust to its rhythms and mood.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: This beautifully shot film explores the female gaze, art, women's empowerment and love. I wish director Sciamma had used more of the tools of filmmaking to entertain the audience so that the final effect was less theoretical and more experiential.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: A patient and intimate portrayal of women finding a space for themselves.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: Even without showing men onscreen, Sciamma depicts the myriad ways in which the patriarchy constricts the lives of her female protagonists.
reviews.author: Rachel Syme

reviews.text: "Portrait of a Lady on Fire" is about the audacity of creation, whether of a new work of art or a new love affair. With precise, confident brushstrokes, Sciamma creates a tender and complex love story of passionate intensity.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Celine Sciamma's subtly erotic period drama is nothing short of a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady On Fire is a film that demands repeat viewings in order to truly unravel the mastery with which Sciamma builds her world, her characters, her exploration of women.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: It's a slow burn, sure, but the embers are remarkable.
reviews.author: Cody Corrall

reviews.text: What I enjoyed about it was the discovery of love.
reviews.author: Karen Krizanovich

reviews.text: Sciamma has fashioned an offbeat period feminist fable that's both visually exquisite and dramatically intoxicating.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Beneath its gloss, "Portrait of a Lady on Fire" is about how women - considered property that can be used as barter in a patriarchal world - cope with the constraints life allows them.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: An erotic, exquisitely articulated lesbian love story.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: It is a film about womanhood, sisterhood, love, marriage and being seen and heard. And it is wonderful.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: It could have been claustrophobic but the central story is so passionately involving you don't want to look elsewhere at all.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: "A man looks, he sees, he reacts," Hitchcock once said... What if the person doing the looking is a woman? Céline Sciamma's elegantly conceived and exquisitely executed Portrait of a Lady on Fire... supplies an answer.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire builds from embers into a raging inferno of emotion in one of the best romance films in ten years.
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: This is a film about looking, female looking specifically.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire, more than being one of the greatest lesbian romances, is a beautiful film about artistic labor and the social contexts that uplift some artists above others.
reviews.author: Justine Smith

reviews.text: Director Celine Sciamma has crafted an impeccably tasteful and rather moving love story.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: In terms of modern sexual politics, it's a pointed celebration of how some female lovers look, see, understand, empathize and argue with, and touch each other.
reviews.author: Graham Fuller

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire explores the permanence of art and the fleeting nature of love, but it also, to my pleasant surprise, touches on elements of female mysticism and magic that were completely unexpected but perfect for the story.
reviews.author: Jessica Mason

reviews.text: A fairly standard, stuffy costume drama.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: It's an all-in effort, and Sciamma has created something of a masterwork. It's a deeply layered story - a brush-up on the story of Orpheus and Eurydice wouldn't hurt - with themes that transcend era and setting. This girl is on fire.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: What a thrillingly versatile film-maker Céline Sciamma has proved to be.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Its uniquely gorgeous tale of 18th century romance features a pair of picture-perfect mademoiselles (Noemie Merlant and Adele Haenel), as a young artist and her initially unwilling subject.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is a romantic gothic drama that will make viewers hearts sing and break in almost equal measure.
reviews.author: Stephen Porzio

reviews.text: By the time the final heartbreaking, all-a-flutter sequence plays out to the strains of Vivaldi, it's been a remarkable sensory journey.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: [Writer/director Céleine] Sciamma's work is an elegant, emotionally-resonant and provocative drama that will mesmerize viewers with its brilliant visuals and deep-seated passion.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: [A] strikingly exquisite film.
reviews.author: June Butler

reviews.text: [I]t's the way the film stealthily transforms this into an exploration of the thrilling yet debilitating grip fleeting moments of intense connection can exert on those who experience them that makes its prolonged final shot so memorable.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Powerful and profoundly beautiful.
reviews.author: Paddy Kehoe

reviews.text: We need a different word for masterpiece.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: Mesmerising, extraordinary, impressive, honest
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: It's about two women falling in love and it's rapturous, scorching, ravishing and will lock your eyes to the screen.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Portrait is a slow burn, a bubbling-up and boiling-over romance that is sure to ignite the soul of anyone who gets too close to its flickering flames.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Beautiful, bold and sensual, it is stunning to watch.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Sciamma's film is the very definition of slow burn, but when it catches, it sets the audience on fire, too.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: With Portrait of a Lady on Fire, Céline Sciamma has crafted a romance which swaps cliche and sentimentality for poignant questions about the nature of image-making and the attempt to capture a memory.
reviews.author: Tom Duggins

reviews.text: The film is at its strongest when [Céline] Sciamma challenges the conventional dynamic between sitter and artist, observed and observer, asking where one ends and the other begins.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: It burns, but in the best possible way.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: A story about love and desire, but also about trust, the role of women and their art in the 18th Century, and of course, the female gaze. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: On the whole, director Céline Sciamma masters the waxing and waning of moods... [But] one takes away Heloise's tousled hair and rich, satiated half-smile, and tends to overlook Sciamma's trouble settling on an ending.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: Sciamma conjures the past with such clarity you clean forget the modern world and the crew crouched in fleeces and headphones just out of shot. Such, done right, is the magic of cinema.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: It's a drop-dead beautiful film to look at too. Tactile, soft and limpid.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Sciamma has crafted a fiercely intelligent love story that's intellectually stimulating and swoon-inducing in equal measures.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: A slow-burn, humane and ultimately tragic telling of its story of forbidden love.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: There are theme-park rides; there is cinema; there are sacred love poems to take with you for the rest of your life. Thank you for giving us the last one, Céline Sciamma.
reviews.author: Sophie Monks Kaufman

reviews.text: ... a revelatory testament of queer desire and resilience.
reviews.author: Erica Ciccarone

reviews.text: It is an incredibly passionate romance.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: It is one of the most one of the most gorgeous films you will ever see in your life. Every single frame of it is like a picture that you want to hang in your home and it is just devastatingly romantic and sad and sexy and beautiful.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: In Sciamma's hands, the camera savors each scene like a moving still-life.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: Merlant and Haenel sizzle in the intoxicating 18th-century love story. The period drama soars to new heights only to deliver a downpour of unbridled passion.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Sciamma's film is even better than Parasite. ... While the latter leans on an absurdist depiction of Tarantino-style orgiastic violence to achieve its climax, Portrait needs but a few deep breaths, a smile and a tear.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire becomes a laboratory in which two actresses and the director try to see what happens when the currently out-of-vogue male gaze vanishes.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: An ode to memories as much as it is to lost love... Portrait of a Lady on Fire is a love story for the ages.
reviews.author: Carmen Paddock

reviews.text: Brightly colored but also cool and crisp; you can feel the brisk sea air in its scenes of women striding along the coast.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Offers much quiet elegance, with more than a handful of beautiful scenes.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: It is a delicious struggle for dominance; a game of feints, flattery and half-truths.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: This is a film that, like the painting at its center, is going to enrapture and galvanize those who look upon it for a long time to come.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: What the film excels at, however, is the anticipatory desire. It builds slowly, concluding with a stunning sequence that is all breathless remembrance and self-satisfaction that is both wordless and impalpable
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: It's a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: An exquisite, exceptional romantic drama.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: You've never seen another movie quite like this. In its quiet gaze, love becomes art.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: The sheer beauty of the storytelling would be remarkable even if the performances, which are both period-apt and urgently contemporary, weren't just as remarkable.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Some may find its method comparable to watching paint dry, but if you can uncover the more profound significance and adjust to its gentle and poetic tone, 'Portrait of a Lady on Fire' will scorch your heart with its impassioned touch.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Sciamma has a keen eye for the ways that women have always cared for each other under the radar of society, dealing with unwanted pregnancies and building little communities in plain sight.
reviews.author: Emily St. James

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire doesn't shout at you. It whispers gently from the porch of another house, leaving its message to be carried on the breeze.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: It's a rare thing to hear a conversation in a movie that makes you sit up a little straighter; it's even rarer that you hear a silence that does the same.
reviews.author: Joshua Rivera

reviews.text: Sumptuously beautiful.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: A deeply romantic film in which two people find love, are pulled apart, and in that day, in that time, couldn't find their way back together.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: A stirring romantic saga. It effortlessly blends the lives of a painter and her subject as if they were two colors on a palette.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: It's so beautiful you might want to see the movie twice, once for the wrenching story, and a second to bask in the most alluring visual experiences you'll likely encounter in a theater.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire perfectly demonstrates how to depict gay love in a period setting without caving to broader societal expectations.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: Sciamma has crafted a divine heartbreaker that only grows in prestige and power the more I keep pondering its many interior convolutions.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Using light, framing and texture the same way a Rococo painter would in 1770, Sciamma has crafted a world that demands to be seen and felt.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: A very regal romance... I think this film is fine and nice. It's very handsome.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: True to its title, "Portrait of a Lady on Fire" generates more than its share of heat, even if it never truly becomes an engulfing flame.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: With Portrait of a Lady on Fire, French filmmaker Céline Sciamma is now four films into an already impressive career, and on the verge of a breakthrough...
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: What a sumptuous, splendid, devastating film. Please don't miss the chance to see it in a theatre.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: This movie is ripe for Valentine's Day viewing.
reviews.author: Emma Baty

reviews.text: Witnessing the act of artistic creation lets the film's audience appreciate the connection between love, desire, and especially memory.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: A haunting examination of love and the restrictions imposed on women by eighteenth-century French society.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: With minimal dialogue from the Cannes Film Festival award-winning screenwriter Céline Sciamma and the gilded, perfectly composed imagery from cinematographer Claire Mathon, the movie presents a feast for the eye and a salve for the heart.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: Céline Sciamma's masterpiece.
reviews.author: Katie Goh

reviews.text: If the film ultimately strikes a false note, that only proves its thesis.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: The woman as property meets the artist who will be responsible for creating the woman as voyeuristic picture.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: The movie's most striking deviation from more traditional period romances is that here power and hierarchy, while they frame the story and must be navigated, are not eroticized.
reviews.author: Lidija Haas

reviews.text: A love story that is both wildly passionate and quietly beautiful, so much so that it doesn't need to be shouted about from the cliffs, as all the character's emotions can be expressed with one look and sometimes, not even that...
reviews.author: Katie Hogan

reviews.text: ...a love story of aching delicacy...
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: The good news is that you will definitely get lucky after going to see this movie. The even better news is that you'll have a ton to talk about afterward.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: The softness and balance in every single frame of Sciamma's observant love story achieve what a great classical painting does, making the viewer consider the subject's unspoken emotions through expression, position and movement.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: I don't know that I've ever seen a film that works so well on both the emotional and intellectual levels.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Céline Sciamma, who previously assayed more contemporary studies with Tomboy and Girlhood, here strikes the perfect balance between smart social parable, formal composition, and soulful contemplation of the tools -- and limits -- of art itself.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady is simmering, sensual, and gorgeously cinematic.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: Love stories are as old as stories themselves, but "Portrait of a Lady on Fire" feels very much like it's inventing something.
reviews.author: Barbara VanDenburgh

reviews.text: It's an emotional journey of two bound by society, but whose love knows no bounds. The final scene is a masterclass in acting and direction; no words are spoken, and it says everything.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: The film is a sensual delight, and not just in the visual contrast of firelight and sunlight, or the women's dresses, russet and emerald. Sciamma has created a sound design that favours the natural...
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Sciamma has a great feel for structure, for emotional arcs, and for pinpoint-accurate catharses that nevertheless preserve the tantalizing enigma of her characters.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Looming over the film is an aching reminder that while women have always exercised agency in whatever capacity they could, the spectre of patriarchy continues to proscribe what women are able to hold for themselves.
reviews.author: Natalia Keogan

reviews.text: Marianne and Héloïse's unfurling of feelings for each other is more than just wish fulfillment; there's an emotional logic to it that believably defies their historical context.
reviews.author: Jas Keimig

reviews.text: A powerful and meticulously crafted film, Portrait of a Lady on Fire is as emotionally wrecking as it is beautiful to look at.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Visually ravishing.
reviews.author: Ben Croll

reviews.text: Sciamma doesn't over-play the sensuality. She uses the stillness to create a deeper intimacy between the two women. And for us, the quiet, and the calm, measured pace of the film draws our attention to their growing bond.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Writer-director Céline Sciamma's soulful filmmaking, alongside her whole team, deserves every success it's had so far.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: What unfolds is an instantly canonical love story for the ages, and I don't make such a claim lightly.
reviews.author: Tre'vell Anderson

reviews.text: [Céline] Sciamma shows us two women who discover the true meaning of beeing seen in a way that profoundly changes their view of themselves and the world around them.
reviews.author: Steven Sheehan

reviews.text: This luscious lesbian romance often recalls classic works of art, Claire Mathon's cinematography rich in her use of color and composition while Sciamma's...screenplay gives her tale a modern edge with her theme of a woman's right to choose.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Films this exquisite are rare and we should appreciate the treasure of seeing a film with cinematography such as this on a big screen.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: Nothing ever stays happy for long, at least not usually for young women in the 1700s, but Portrait of a Lady on Fire finds so many ways to show us these women as people and not stock figures of their time.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: The most affecting love story of 2019.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The acting by Noémie Merlant and Adèle Haenel is excellent. The love between their characters, Marianne and Héloïse is quite believable, as is the pain and anguish caused by the circumstances of their forbidden love.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: I don't remember the last time I was pulled into a quiet film this arrestingly. Hence, this is one of those cinematic treats to be remembered, not regretted.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire works most sublimely in its aesthetic construction, though, as its fire-and-water motif engulfs viewers while evading cheap drama or fatalism.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: A film of haunting beauty and searing emotions, Portrait of a Lady on Fire is an extraordinary cinematic achievement.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: It's about women finding a voice, finding the agency ... to sketch out a life and an identity for themselves ... it's beautiful to look at, and beautiful to listen to ... I kinda loved it.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: What makes it so special is not just their affair, but the way art plays such a part in it. The two women share a bond that is physical, certainly, but their connection over the aesthetics of artistic expression becomes the truer core of their bond.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: An impeccably detailed, beautifully acted, refined drama with a strong feminist angle that's as stirring as it is thought-provoking.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Portrait Of A Lady On Fire is erotic, but not in the male-gazy (ph) way of movies...
reviews.author: John Powers

reviews.text: A contemporary myth. A must in the history of the cinema. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: Each frame feels like it belongs in The Louvre, hanging alongside the great artists. Few cinematographers capture so much emotion and artistic merit within a single shot.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Some may see it as slow but this is a careful, skilfully assembled drama where it feels every scene and every image has been thought through in immaculate detail.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Writer-director Céline Sciamma (one of the hottest talents in French cinema right now) captures these subtle, yet potent mood swings with an intensity of feeling that continues to deepen throughout.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: A spellbinding cinematic romance where constraint shadows hope and a harsh ending threatens from the tender beginning.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: It's a quiet, meditative film that is indeed beautiful to, yes, gaze upon while you ponder its subtle yet powerful accumulation of thoughts and questions.
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: Céline Sciamma has created a film that is both beautiful and intelligent, sensual and intellectually stimulating, but, above all, a totally feminist film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: There is an intoxicating stillness to this drama, an attention to silence and evocative, dreamlike sounds -- brushstrokes, crackling flames, waves against the shoreline -- that suggest everything is playing out in a detached and sacred space.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: ...has a great sense of time and place, and, most appropriately for a film about art, the cinematography is exquisitely painterly.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: The screenplay, for which Sciamma deservedly won a prize at Cannes, is so compelling not for how it radically alters the genre but for how it surprises and intrigues within it.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Portrait, winner of the Best Screenplay award at Cannes this year, depicts the aspirations, hopes and dreams of its female characters and explores them with intimacy and loving insight.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: An intense, headily sensual epic with a sometimes overcooked feel and oodles of Euro-artiness.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: The painting that Marianne creates is like the film. The more details we accumulate, the deeper we are immersed into the thoughts and emotions of the women.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: It was a privilege to have seen and experienced Portrait of a Lady on Fire.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: This movie. This movie. I'm going to write more about it shortly, but now two days after watching it, I cannot believe how good it is.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: Despite the contained setting, the film has an epic quality, as well as a romantic intensity that marks a major leap forward from Sciamma's previous films Tomboy and Water Lillies.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: The emotional storm that will sweep two women away comes most strikingly alive through what they leave unsaid.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: The story is quite simple, but it brims with desire. Sciamma could have relied on the strength of that alone.
reviews.author: Kristen Yoonsoo Kim

reviews.text: An unabashed masterpiece, something that feels like it's already survived decades of adoration to be heralded as one of the great art films.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: This is a once in a lifetime love that frustration and resentment can risk destroying in hindsight as long as the memory of what was shared becomes permanent in their hearts.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Without a doubt, this is my favorite film of the year. Céline Sciamma perfectly captures the slow magic of falling in love for the first time.
reviews.author: Lindsay Pugh

reviews.text: Sciamma's work with the actors here reflects an inspired effort-going far beyond costume and décor-to evoke the inner life of the historical period.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Anyone who has ever felt burning passion for another person will relate to and fall for this spine-tingling work.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: This is a rare film that takes the breath away with moments of transcendent beauty.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Try to watch and not feel a bit on fire yourself.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: This is a film I admired more than I liked... I just found the film to be too hyper-staged and too artfully constructed to make an emotional connection.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: It's a visual masterpiece... The cinematography by Claire Mathon is stunning [and] the acting is wonderful.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: It's a period drama of burning intensity that brilliantly captures the collaboration of creator and muse through its gaze. Sciamma delivers a bittersweet, subversive, and honest depiction of lesbian love of the highest caliber.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: As steamy and sumptuous as its setting is cold and remote, Portrait of a Lady on Fire is a love story born out of the act of looking -- and of being seen.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: The connection between Merlant and Haenel is just electric - the way they look at each other? Damn. "Get you a person who looks at you the way Haenel looks at Merlant" is a meme I'm gonna make.
reviews.author: Jaime Davis

reviews.text: An exquisite period piece about love between headstrong women, with a large dollop of art theory to boot.
reviews.author: Jenni Miller

reviews.text: Fact is, Sciamma doesn't trust the expressiveness of her medium; despite deft technique, she stages obvious agitprop.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Heloise and Marianne, and the way their ardor is allowed to slowly unfold onscreen is both heartwarming and, given the dismal prospects for a future together, heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: If the film lurches at times with schematic dudgeon-devolving into a checklist of coolly outraged points to be made-it also gloriously blooms as a tale of lesbian ardor.
reviews.author: Melissa Anderson

reviews.text: Should a painting capture its subject or liberate her?
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Writer/director Céline Sciamma takes her time with Portrait of a Lady on Fire, and the results are mysterious, romantic, and quietly devastating.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Though the film sizzles with an erotic heat that grows from initial repression, Sciamma is not pedaling softcore lesbian porn. Her transfixing film, about the heady experience of an impossible first love, is a timeless work of art.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: A subtle and thrilling love story, at once unsentimental in its realistic assessment of women's circumstances and almost utopian in its celebration of the freedom that is nonetheless available to them.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire -- the fire is figurative, but also real -- goes beyond painterly beauty. It sees into souls.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: It's a relic out of time, creating a lush, erotic world out of glances and small movements; yet it's also very much of our time.
reviews.author: Andrew Lapin

reviews.text: This film is a work of art and the catalyst for this masterpiece of female filmmaking is lesbian love. It is a sensual, passionate period piece where each frame is visually composed worthy of being put-on display in any gallery.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: What makes it a great movie, rather than a list of ideologically correct imperatives, is the specificity and delicacy with which Sciamma has shaped the material - the way each new idea seems to emerge from the love story like a whisper.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: This gorgeous movie was tapped by the NY Film Critics Circle for Best Cinematography and by folks at the Cannes Festival for Best Screenplay. This slowly deepening look at lesbianism in a remote 18th century section of France is a gem.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: This is not just a film about love between women, but a rumination on the sacredness of a feminine space and the nature of art created by and for women.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: I can assure you that it has affected me like no other film this year and I sincerely recommend you seek it out as it becomes more widely available in the coming months.
reviews.author: Sean O'Rourke

reviews.text: Like a rocky shore at dusk or the bloom of first love, it's something that needs to be experienced rather than described.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: In a film told with sweeping visual scope, Sciamma plunges the viewer into a story and setting of the deepest intimacy.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Sciamma's gift to 2019 sets a highest standard for any romance that will come after it.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire... is an unforgettable love story that unspools at a slow burn until the final act, which blazes with an incandescence.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Quiet yet filled with intensity, Portrait of a Lady on Fire nails the physicality and emotions associated with mutual unspoken attraction. It's a slow burn - pun intended - as it builds their relationship, but the pay off is absolutely worth the wait.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is that rare movie in which every choice feels thought through, meaningful, and right, from the costumes by Dorothée Guiraud to the cinematography by Claire Mathon.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Every frame is immaculate.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: Arresting the senses and stimulating the mind, Céline Sciamma has made one of the most breathtaking screen romances of the decade...
reviews.author: Chris Feil

reviews.text: It couldn't be fresher if it were mixed on a palette in front of us, and the intensity with which, in the second half, the two women look themselves into love, as it were, is fleshly, funny, and sublimely untheoretical.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Every scene, spoken word of dialogue, and display of body language is crucial and informative to writer and director Céline Sciamma's slow-scorching Portrait of a Lady on Fire
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is an exquisite film. A period piece which was conceived of and directed by a woman, features a cast which is almost exclusively female and gives those who watch it a window into the heart and mind of women.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: Its expressions of what art can signify -- how much a look can carry, what power is contained in the making of an image (and who gets to make it) -- don't just resonate. They're revolutionary.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: It's a quiet and deceptively slow film, at times featuring so little sound that one can almost hear the characters' hearts fluttering. The pay-off, in a final 20 minutes of simply exquisite, cathartic cinema, is one for the history books.
reviews.author: Tom Augustine

reviews.text: Do yourself a favour and bask at the fire of Sciamma's film, because it is a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Toby Woollaston

reviews.text: This is a formal, beautiful, disciplined and mature film from a writer/director who seemingly can't put a foot wrong.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: The most beautiful thing about this film is that it captures how we remember love, how we turn it into a pure memory that no one, not even social conventions, can touch. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergi Sánchez

reviews.text: Portrait is a masterly work of historical realism done in high-flying poetic style.
reviews.author: Erica Abeel

reviews.text: It's hard to call Sciamma's vision anything short of a triumph on nearly every level. It starts off as enticing and mysterious, but quickly transports the viewer into an even deeper stupor of romance.
reviews.author: Owen Butler

reviews.text: It's an altogether quiet, understated affair that only betrays the fiery emotions burning underneath at the very end.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: In its plastic beauty 'Portrait of a Lady on Fire' is also the perfect story of the encounter of two souls in search of their happiness. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire brims with the unique burning desire and adoration that the female gaze can capture.
reviews.author: Stefania Sarrubba

reviews.text: Despite being a period film, Portrait of a Lady on Fire avoids the stigmas and mannerisms of those films and remains paused and melodic in its portrayal of romance. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Quim Casas

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire plays, at first, like a song with missed notes - until eventually, it discovers and carefully re-assembles them, revealing, in its final scene, the music of the soul.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The film never stops, until reaching its two beautiful consecutive endings, growing in emotion, culminating the sublimation of the spirit. The utopia of a tragic love on the edge of the precipice. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: We see how each avoided glance, each rejected caress and, of course, that emotional ending, is presented as an analysis of the emphasized epistemologies and bifurcated moralisms. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: After a visually dazzling and nimble first half, the momentum deflates in the second hour as the film becomes more conventional.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire recognises that within its love story the women at the centre (and the women around them) are nuanced people who contain multitudes.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Real love may be fleeting, but as Portrait of a Lady on Fire explains, art and memory are immortal.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: The perfect word to describe Portrait of a Lady on Fire is nonchalant.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is a heartrending and sensual tale of longing, female solidarity, and heartache that is thrillingly performed by its cast and vividly directed by Celine Sciamma. A love story for the ages.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: Sciamma knows there's beauty to be found within a stifling environment.
reviews.author: Juan Barquin

reviews.text: A devastating watch that is likely to linger long after you've witnessed its goodbye.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Not only is this easily one of the best films I've seen this year, this decade even, but it's one of the few essential works that demonstrates what cinema as an art form - as a language - is capable of.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is an immaculately executed simmering Queer love story-gorgeous in image, and rendered in fine detail to the female gaze.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire has well written dialogue and is sumptuously filmed, each shot tells a story.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: Céline Sciamma's gorgeous, heart-wrenching Portrait of a Lady on Fire screened on the first day of TIFF, and it became the gold standard by which I evaluated all other films.
reviews.author: Alex Heeney

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is hyper-aware of the perils of its setting, and yet still manages to be inherently sexy, thanks to the chemistry of its leads.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: Writer/director Celine Sciamma has created something truly remarkable, a cinematic masterpiece that needs to be seen multiple times, but that in even a single viewing sounds an emotional vibrato deep within the viewer.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: Peak *clap* Lesbian *clap* Cinema.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: This is cinema distilled to the minute, and characters whose visible inner lives can take on the immortalized quality of a mural's subject.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: The excellence of all involved allows Portrait of a Lady on Fire to be not only one of the year's best films, but also quite simply a timeless love story.
reviews.author: Matthew Singleton

reviews.text: A surprising sense of detail in which each small gesture seems important. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jonay Armas

reviews.text: Céline Sciamma's tender masterpiece paints a portrait of visual poetry, of what happens when art intersects with love for a fragment of time.
reviews.author: Monique Vigneault

reviews.text: Sciamma's control of the auditory aspects of her film yields an ending that will stagger anyone with a full heart.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: [Céline] Sciamma's original screenplay offers a surprising romance.
reviews.author: Lisa Nesselson

reviews.text: The type of film you fall swiftly in love with, and like the memory of an old lover, stays with you long after.
reviews.author: Oliver Whitney

reviews.text: A work of art that is equally beautiful and heartbreaking, Portrait of a Lady on Fire is an exquisite love story.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: A vapid and burdensome experience in spite of its beauty.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: gorgeous and mesmerizing film. Noémie Merlant and Adèle Haenel bring an intensity that is simply awe inspiring.
reviews.author: Raquel Stecher

reviews.text: Aesthetically pleasing 18th-century period piece drama on desire.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: The craft of the film is undeniable, but with a central romance that never becomes the emotionally resonant experience it is set up to be, no amount of skilled assemblage can make Portrait of a Lady on Fire more than a beautiful decoration.
reviews.author: Anna Swanson

reviews.text: The film could be considered Exhibit A for essays on the female gaze.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Simply one of the year's best.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: This absolute marvel of a movie is not to be missed.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire feels like a flawless film.
reviews.author: Beth McDonough

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is about portraits and the secrets they hide, those hidden in plain sight, only accessbile to those who follow the clues.
reviews.author: Shelagh Rowan-Legg

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire is as smart as it as emotionally trenchant.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: A smoldering, graceful complicated love story that illustrates the best of women thanks to director Céline Sciamma and exquisite performances by Noémie Merlant and Adèle Haenel. A definite must-see for the awards season!
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: It is so very easy to label a film incendiary, but Portrait of a Lady on Fire deserves the scalding honour. It will ignite every flame you might have.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: French director Celine Sciamma gives us a beautiful allegory of love as portrait-painting, in this emotionally compelling, lyrical story of two women who fall in love by gazing into each other's eyes
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: So irresistible is the pull between Marianne and Héloïse that it's hard to know whether to describe Portrait of a Lady on Fire as an erotically-charged romance or romantically-charged erotica.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: A film for the senses as much as the mind and heart, Portrait of a Lady on Fire continues to solidify Sciamma's status as one of the most exciting and accomplished filmmakers working in Europe today.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: What's most stirring about Céline Sciamma's film is the lack of artifice in Héloïse and Marianne's feelings for one another.
reviews.author: Christopher Gray

reviews.text: Sciamma dodges any hint of melodrama, opting to treat emotions delicately and faithfully for a time that suppressed them into glances and gestures rather than pouring them out into words.
reviews.author: Isabel Stevens

reviews.text: One of the most extraordinary aspects of the film is how the passionate romance between these two characters differs from those in the many movies we've seen about male artists and their female subjects or muses.
reviews.author: Amy Taubin

reviews.text: Led by fantastic performances, genuine bouts of romance and passion, brilliantly sparse visual storytelling, effortless direction and a shockingly powerful emotional punch, Portrait of a Lady on Fire is the best film of 2019.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Defiantly progressive in its perception of love and creation that sees the two parties on an equal footing, Portrait of a Lady on Fire is as poignant as it is invigorating.
reviews.author: Elena Lazic

reviews.text: A rapt, delicate love story between two corseted women isolated from the world.
reviews.author: Kong Rithdee

reviews.text: Portrait de la jeune fille en feu - a study of two women pursuing lives larger than the ones they've been given - chooses the spirit over formalism; poetry over realism; myth over history.
reviews.author: Rebecca Liu

reviews.text: Sciamma demonstrates that she has developed a sharp finesse as a narrator. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: Four out of four. It's the number of great films directed by the French Céline Sciamma. The last, Portrait of a Lady on Fire, is the most sublime of all. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire does not so much invent something new, but captures something as timeless and tragic as a first love-one that percolates with the sadness of an inevitable goodbye.
reviews.author: Leonardo Goi

reviews.text: The film supports interest in the contribution of two notable actresses for what is ultimately a more than interesting story written, directed and starring exclusively women. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: What follows is both a guided study of the process of creation and the very meaning of the film contemplated. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: With brush strokes of a deeply pictorial, elegant and sober photograph, Sciamma constructs an honest portrait of the femininity of the time that transmits truth, free of all affected artifice. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sara Martínez Ruiz

reviews.text: This movie is a full cinematic experience and deserves to be viewed on the big screen so an audience can immerse themselves in the sublime.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: No longer is Sciamma dealing with the struggles of young people as they deal with their changing bodies, but she is taking the logical next step, crafting a romance all around the idea of capturing the female body in a work of art.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: If Call Me By Your Name is a finished piece, Portrait of a Lady on Fire is the process behind it: the scribbled notes; the sketched outline; the first lick of paint.
reviews.author: Gus Edgar

reviews.text: Haenel brings her turbulent presence to Héloïse, but with a degree of era-appropriate restraint that makes her moments of vulnerability and rebellion all the more distressing.
reviews.author: Manuela Lazic

reviews.text: It's as if Marianne and Héloïse's story lives in the finite window of a neverending golden hour, shining only for them.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: It's a great example of how a well-told story, with vivid characters, can seep right into your bones and keep you thinking for days afterward-and the pleasure felt while watching it isn't negligible either.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: A film that invades your mind, body, and soul as the 18th century hypnotizes you into a romantic trance like a sunset lullaby.
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: In [writer-director Céline] Sciamma's gifted hands, the film escapes cliché and becomes something glorious - a study of forbidden love that grandly highlights how much has been lost under the crush of hetero patriarchy.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: This is simply a beautiful film to behold, with exquisite attention to detail and lighting.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: The film has a sobriety and subtlety. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: The range of themes presented by this delicate film is impressive. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: Portrait of a Lady on Fire there is... a subversion of the stories told so many times. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Violeta Kovacsics

reviews.text: Makes us continue to look forward to [director Céline Sciamma's] next works. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos F. Heredero

reviews.text: Fittingly for a film about a painter, the compositions are glorious: the use of a rich and diverse colour palette; the perfectly framed mise en scene and the feel for texture and material as well as the softness of skin and the body.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: If you miss the crashing waves and sexual longing of The Piano, and think Carol could have used a bit more Call Me By Your Name, then Portrait Of A Lady On Fire will set your world alight.
reviews.author: Anna Smith

reviews.text: [Céline] Sciamma's love story deserves to be recognised as its own incredible take on queerness, love, and the power of art to communicate both.
reviews.author: Tom Bond

reviews.text: Sciamma has a magnificent capability for elegant prose that wouldn't feel out of place in a classic novel, the kind of dialogue that simmers long after it is spoken.
reviews.author: Caroline Tsai

reviews.text: Almost every scene in the second half builds sensationally on the last.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Far from some stuffy costume drama, it's a deeply stirring romance with a modern soul, and also a forcefully, compassionately feminist one...
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: For all of its composed sumptuousness, Portrait of a Lady on Fire makes for thrilling viewing.
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: A masterpiece, pure and simple. Céline Sciamma returns to Cannes with a stunning film everyone should experience.
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: Not a moment in Portrait of a Lady on Fire is wasted, which suits a story about lovers without a moment to lose.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: It's a film that captures the feeling you get from the last scene of "Roman Holiday" and stretches it over a full two hours in which not a single moment is wasted.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: This is an incredibly tense and erotic movie.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: There is a clear and cogent subtext here about how women were portrayed in the past and what they were allowed to portray, but Sciamma never gets on her soapbox or allows the dialogue to become didactic.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: Sciamma's ravishing celebration of female passion and desire is rooted in mutual sexual awakening but ultimately becomes a story of a much deeper, more spiritual kind of love.
reviews.author: Adam Woodward

reviews.text: What did it remind me of? De Laclos' Dangerous Liaisons? Nicolas Roeg's Bad Timing? I don't know. But what a story of desire.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: "Portrait" dares to engage directly with the questions of representation and gender that seem to have flummoxed the film industry of late, broadening its focus to the subject of womanhood itself at a time documented almost exclusively by men.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Céline Sciamma's first foray into period drama starts out as a cautiously demure watercolour wash but gradually builds into a vivid, full-blooded oil portrait of the stolen romantic relationship between two young women.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

synopsis: In 1770 the young daughter of a French countess develops a mutual attraction to the female artist commissioned to paint her wedding portrait.
